topic: Rather than just an informational application I want one that I can access from anywhere, so in github pages, that serves as a navigation and education site for all things for a small business whose primary business is supporting federal government programs ... a source for walking me through any path available for doing business with the federal government and of course large primes and other partnering arrangements. Also built into this I'd like a search capability that finds opportunities from these various sites.
question: For a small business that wants federal work, what routes exist (direct contracts and set-asides, contract vehicles, SBIR/STTR and other R&D funding, Other Transactions and Commercial Solutions Openings, and work through primes and partners), what does each require, how does the government on the other side of the table actually buy, and what has changed in 2025-26 that the official pages have not caught up with?

in: the four route families: SBIR/STTR and innovation front doors; set-asides, certifications and contract vehicles; primes and partnering; Other Transactions, consortia and CSOs
the government buyer's side: the six AAF pathways, the civilian procurement model, the grants model, each agency's small-business office and forecast
the gates: registrations, representations, cybersecurity, accounting, clearance, export, bonding, labor, payment
what changed in 2025-26: the FAR overhaul, the Warfighting Acquisition System, the SBIR/STTR reauthorization, 8(a) reform, CMMC, the FY2026 NDAA
free help: APEX Accelerators, SBA partners, agency outreach
what large primes say on their own supplier pages, recorded as stated
out: foreign military sales and export licensing beyond the registration gate
grants other than SBIR/STTR (they appear in search results only)
anything tailored to a specific firm
recommendations of paid consultants, tools or memberships

interview.q: Is this meant to be tailored to one firm, or a generic guide any small federal contractor could use?
interview.answer: NO it should not have any connection whatsoever to CohesionForce. ANY small contractor should be able to use this.
I'll want to name this thing "FAR Out"

interview.q: How should the spine be organised?
interview.answer: Situation-first: a pathfinder asks where the firm is and leads into a catalogue of the four route families.

interview.q: Which route families in depth for the first release?
interview.answer: All four: SBIR/STTR and front doors; OTs, consortia, CSOs; set-asides and vehicles; primes and partnering.
Layered: plain language first, expanding to rule citations and detail.
Topic-mode prototype now, with extension files.

interview.q: Recheck per family or once over all four?
interview.answer: Lets do that then (one recheck over all four families).
